title: Je veux être ton agent  (I Want to Be Your Agent)

segments.t: On a small black stage, under a single spotlight, Sofia performed in a strange, poetic play called 'Absence', full of lines about loss, waiting and doubt. Now the show is over, and Gabriel walks her out into the street. Listen to it in French first. Let the words go by; the meaning will come. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Tu es venu! C'est incroyable!
Je ne t'ai pas vu avant la fin.
Tu as aimé les autres? Ils sont bien, non?
Oui, ils sont bons.
Mais c'est surtout toi. Tu étais magnifique.
Merci, Gabriel. Merci d'être venu.
C'est moi qui dois te remercier.
Tu es une vraie comédienne.
Merci infiniment.
Au revoir, Gabriel. À demain.
Sofia? Attends.
Je veux être ton agent.
Tu es sérieux?
Oui, je suis sérieux.
Je n'ai pas beaucoup de travail, tu sais.
Je vais t'aider à trouver du travail.
D'accord. Très bien!
Let's walk back through it. Sofia is still buzzing from the show, and she can hardly believe her eyes.
Tu es venu! C'est incroyable!
'You came! I can't believe it!' Literally 'it's unbelievable'. The first action word is in the past, built with 'to be', because coming is a movement.
Je ne t'ai pas vu avant la fin.
'I didn't see you until the end.' Literally 'before the end'. The little word for 'you' sits before the helper word, inside the 'not'.
Tu as aimé les autres?
'Did you like the others?' The past tense with 'to have' and the past form of 'to like'.
Ils sont bien, non?
'They're good, aren't they?' Adding the word for 'no' at the end is the easy French way to say 'aren't they?' or 'right?'.
Oui, ils sont bons.
'Yes, they're good.' Gabriel is polite about the rest of the cast.
Mais c'est surtout toi. Tu étais magnifique.
'But it's mostly you. You were wonderful.' The past form for 'you were' describes how she was on stage, a lasting state.
Merci, Gabriel. Merci d'être venu.
'Thank you, Gabriel. Thank you for coming.' After 'thank you for', French uses 'to have come', not 'coming'. The little word in front is 'for', shortened before a vowel.
C'est moi qui dois te remercier.
'I'm the one who should thank you.' Literally 'it's me who must thank you'. The same trick to put weight on one person.
Tu es une vraie comédienne.
'You're a real actress.' The words for 'real' and 'actress' both have feminine endings. This means a lot to Sofia, who spends her days answering phones.
Merci infiniment.
'Thank you so much.' Literally 'thank you infinitely'. A very warm thank-you.
Au revoir, Gabriel. À demain.
'Bye, Gabriel. See you tomorrow.' Tomorrow she'll be back behind the reception desk. She starts to walk away.
Sofia? Attends.
'Sofia? Wait.' A casual command, because they use the casual 'you' with each other.
Je veux être ton agent.
'I want to be your agent.' The verb 'to want', then the plain verb 'to be'. It's the big moment of the scene.
Tu es sérieux?
'Are you serious?' A question made just by the voice going up at the end.
Oui, je suis sérieux.
'Yes, I'm serious.' Gabriel means it.
Je n'ai pas beaucoup de travail, tu sais.
'I don't have much work, you know.' After 'not', 'a lot of' becomes 'much'. Same words in French: literally 'not a lot of work'.
Je vais t'aider à trouver du travail.
'I'm going to help you find work.' The verb 'to go' plus another verb for the near future again, and after 'help', a little word for 'to' before the next verb.
D'accord. Très bien!
'Okay. Great!' Two of the most useful words in French, and Sofia has a real agent at last. Here's the whole scene again, from the top.
Tu es venu! C'est incroyable!
Je ne t'ai pas vu avant la fin.
Tu as aimé les autres? Ils sont bien, non?
Oui, ils sont bons.
Mais c'est surtout toi. Tu étais magnifique.
Merci, Gabriel. Merci d'être venu.
C'est moi qui dois te remercier.
Tu es une vraie comédienne.
Merci infiniment.
Au revoir, Gabriel. À demain.
Sofia? Attends.
Je veux être ton agent.
Tu es sérieux?
Oui, je suis sérieux.
Je n'ai pas beaucoup de travail, tu sais.
Je vais t'aider à trouver du travail.
D'accord. Très bien!
A happy ending for Sofia, but not for the agency. See you next time!
Bonne journée!
